features.name: share_comments_technical_vocab
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments use technical or academic vocabulary (e.g., methodology, empirical, correlation, hypothesis)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of counter-argument comments by other users. For each comment, decide whether the commenter's own wording uses technical/academic vocabulary of the kind exemplified by methodology, empirical, correlation, hypothesis (scholarly/scientific/statistical/analytic terms). Ordinary everyday words do not count; mere quoted text attributed to someone else and not adopted by the commenter does not count. Ignore any text announcing OP view change, delta awards, or outcome reports; these are not evidence. Output the number of qualifying comments divided by total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; malformed/missing gives null.

h0: share_comments_technical_vocab has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: Higher share_comments_technical_vocab is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Comments are unordered, have no individual outcomes, so a row-level share is used. The vocabulary category is open-ended ('etc.'); the LLM judges it from the examples given. OC_comments may contain delta/outcome announcements; the prompt excludes them as evidence, but residual contamination risk remains. Rows with no comments get null.
